public_rationale: The research shows why fluent performance alone cannot establish coherent understanding. It also shows that a GPT-style model can learn a usable internal representation. Neither finding settles whether contemporary GPT lacked the broad, transferable understanding Marcus attributes to seven-year-olds. The cited studies concern earlier systems and narrower tasks.
limitations: The behavioral reading of 'faking it' is an evaluator interpretation.
Evidence of one representation cannot establish child-like understanding across domains.
Failures on selected tasks cannot establish the absence of a world model.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Unlike a seven-year-old, GPT lacks a rich model of the world and is just faking it.

statement.excerpt: More than that, any normal seven-year old develops a rich model of the world, including the objects they see, the people they interact with and so on, and even how their bodies work. GPT is still just faking it.
statement.document_title: Three years on, ChatGPT still isn't what it was cracked up to be – and it probably never will be

from_speaker: a rich model of the world
GPT is still just faking it
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that typically developing seven-year-olds possess coherent, transferable understanding of physical, social and bodily situations that contemporary GPT lacks.
'Faking it' is read as producing convincing answers without comparable robust understanding, not as a claim about conscious deception.
The surrounding discussion identifies GPT-5 as the principal contemporary comparison.
An isolated model error would not establish the absence of a rich world model. A narrow internal representation would not establish child-like breadth.
The claim describes current capability. With no reporting cycle specified, the target period is November 2025 through the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Comparative evidence shows typically developing seven-year-olds reasoning coherently across unfamiliar physical, social and bodily situations while contemporary GPT systematically fails to transfer the relevant understanding; representation studies provide consistent additional evidence.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence shows contemporary GPT possessing coherent representations and child-comparable transfer across the stated domains. Narrow successes alone do not meet this condition.

evidence.explanation: The experiments support distinguishing apparent task competence from coherent representations and transfer. They do not establish the claimed absence in November 2025 GPT or compare it with seven-year-olds.

The Othello experiments found a usable internal board representation in a specially trained GPT variant. This challenges a blanket absence-of-representations reading, but does not demonstrate a contemporary GPT model with a child's broad understanding.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Broad, controlled comparisons of the relevant GPT version with seven-year-olds on novel physical, social and bodily reasoning, combined with model-specific representation and transfer tests. A clearer threshold for 'rich' would reduce interpretive uncertainty.
